title: Heartburn medicine review

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. James. How can I help you today?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh, hi, Dr. Smith. I was updating my medication list that I keep at home with all the changes

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: we made during my last appointment with you. And it got me wondering whether I still needed

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: to take the Lenzaprazole. I'm not really sure why I'm taking it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: OK, well, I'm so glad to hear that you keep an updated medication list at home. That's

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: very important for all the healthcare providers who provide prescription for you so that they

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: remain on the same page. But as far as the Lenzaprazole is concerned, it's usually used

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: to treat heartburn. Do you remember when it first may have been prescribed?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yes, I do remember it. It started a couple of years ago when I was in the hospital with

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: pneumonia. Now that you mention it, I do remember having a few days of heartburn while I was there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: OK, and what about more recently and right now? Have you had any more heartburn?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No, I haven't had any heartburn since I left the hospital.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: OK, so that's very good to hear. Just looking at your medical chart here, I don't see any other

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: obvious reason why you would need to stay on the Lenzaprazole. But just to be sure, let me

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: double check by asking you a few questions. So have you had a bleeding ulcer? No, never.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: OK, very good. And otherwise, have you had a scope or have you been told that you have severe

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: esophagitis or something we call Barrett's esophagus? No. OK, that's also very good. So

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: looking at your medication list as well, I don't see any prescribed anti-inflammatories.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Do you happen to take any anti-inflammatories that are over-the-counter products? And by this,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I mean either aspirin or ibuprofen or naprosyn. No. OK, so in this case,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: so in that case, based on the information that I have and what you've just told me,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I don't think there's any indication for you to stay on the Lenzaprazole.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And in fact, sometimes the side effects with this medication, as with many others, outweigh the

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: benefit. The side effects of Lenzaprazole include interfering with absorption of vitamins and

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: minerals from your food. It may increase your risk of developing infections like pneumonia,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: and it gives you a small but increased risk of breaking a bone.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Well, I was not aware of all that. What I'd really like to do is to do everything I can

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: do to avoid having pneumonia gain. OK, sounds like a good plan. So

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: there are a few options that we could consider for how we might stop the Lenzaprazole.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So the first option would be to stop it outright, but use it on demand, we say. So that would mean

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: if you happen to develop more heartburn or reflux symptoms, you could then use it as needed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And then hopefully over time, your symptoms would then go away and you could stop it for good.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: The second option would be to simply decrease the medication to a lower dose for a couple of weeks

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: and see how you do with that. And if your symptoms do not come back, we could then consider

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: stopping it altogether and you could at that point use it on demand. The third option would be to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: switch to a less powerful acid reducer and then see how you do over a couple of weeks

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: and then stop that outright. That's a lot of options. I'm not sure which way would be best

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: for me to go. Could you tell me some of the pros and cons of each of those options?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: OK, absolutely. So for the first option, that was the on demand use. So only taking it when

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: you have symptoms. This generally results in taking fewer pills per week and possibly lower

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: cost. But about one in 10 people may have their symptoms come back. But the second option,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: which involved reducing the less off result to a lower dose and then stopping it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: It does not usually result in symptoms coming back compared to continuing at your current dose.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So that's good news. And lowering the dose can reduce the number of pills you take daily

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: and sometimes reduces side effects and prevents rebound heartburn.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: For the third option, that was changing the medication to another acid reducer we call

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Renididine. About one in five people do have their symptoms come back with this option,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: but it can also help prevent rebound heartburn. Do you think you have a preference for which

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: option you'd like to choose? Well, I think I would prefer lowering the dose and then stopping it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I have a really busy couple of weeks coming up and I don't really want to have to risk

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: having heartburn or reflux again. Okay, sounds like a good approach.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So in that case, since you're taking 30 milligrams daily right now, the Lenzol-Prisol,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: what we could simply do is reduce it to 15 milligram daily for two weeks.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And I could write a prescription for you and you could take that to your pharmacy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: That sounds really good. Is there anything else I should look for?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay, that's a great question. So you should probably keep an eye out for any

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: new reflux symptoms or heartburn, any abdominal pain or feelings of indigestion.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And what should I do if my symptoms come back?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So again, good question. If your symptoms come back, but are only occasional or mild,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: you could consider taking an over-the-counter acid reducer, such as Tums or Gaviscon.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Also, avoiding meals two to three hours before going to bed, as well as raising the head of the

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: bed may help. If your symptoms come back and are bothering you for more than a few days,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: it would be a good idea to let me know and to book a follow-up appointment at that point.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Otherwise, if your symptoms do not come back, I would still recommend that you consider booking

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: a follow-up visit for me in about a month's time. Does that sound reasonable?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yes, thank you. I think the information you give me is very, very helpful. Thank you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay. Do you have any other questions for me at this point?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No, not right now. Okay, sounds good.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So if you do have questions that come to mind, please don't hesitate to contact us here at the

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: office. Thank you very much. That sounds very good and I appreciate your help.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh, my pleasure, Mrs. James. Nice to see you again. Have a good day.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Thank you. You're welcome.
